title: Going Under (Aggro Crab, 2020)
lede: A satirical dungeon-crawler about failed tech startups, whose characters and office spaces take the style’s colors and shapes into 3D.
summary: A 3D game that parodies startup culture with the style’s pastel palette, blob furniture, and bright-skinned characters. 2020.

evidence.note: Inspected two 1920 × 1080 screenshots from the Steam store API (a boss fight and the company lobby). No image is stored.

styles.note: Partial fit: a parody in 3D. It uses the style’s palette, pill-shaped furniture, and potted plants, and blue-skinned monsters, but it has painted texture and 3D light, not flat vector fills.

context: Steam describes it as “a satirical dungeon crawler about exploring the cursed ruins of failed tech startups”, with the player as an unpaid intern in the city of Neo-Cascadia. Developer Aggro Crab, publisher Team17, released 24 September 2020. [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1154810/Going_Under/).
Reviews and essays describe its art as a parody of Corporate Memphis, for example [Merry-Go-Round Magazine](https://merrygoroundmagazine.com/going-under-reclaims-corporate-aesthetics/).
observed: The lobby screenshot shows pink and peach walls, a green floor with orange paths, and long yellow and purple pill-shaped benches.
Rounded teal trees stand in violet pots on red bases; giant soda cans float over a fountain.
The boss screenshot shows a violet brick room with a zig-zag stripe, and a large monster with blue arms and an orange body.
Surfaces carry a brushed, speckled texture and soft 3D shading.
interpretation: Going Under shows how recognizable the style became by 2020: a game could use its palette and props as shorthand for startup culture and make fun of it.
borrow: For a satirical or self-aware brand, keep the style’s palette and props but add texture to signal distance from it.
